questions.q: What is the atomicity of Chlorine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Diatomic. Key Points

• Chlorine exists as a diatomic molecule, which means it consists of two atoms of chlorine joined by a covalent bond.

• The symbol for chlorine is Cl, and its atomic number is 17, which means it has 17 protons and 17 electrons in its nucleus and shells, respectively.

• Chlorine is a halogen, and it is a highly reactive nonmetal that can form compounds with many other elements.

Additional Information

• Tetra-atomic is a rare type of molecule that consists of four atoms of the same or different elements.

• Examples include sulfur tetrafluoride (SF4) and phosphorus tetraiodide (PI4).

• Poly-atomic molecules are common in chemistry and include many organic compounds such as glucose (C6H12O6) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).

• Monoatomic elements are rare and include noble gases such as helium (He) and neon (Ne), which exist as single atoms and do not form molecules with other atoms.

questions.q: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis. Key Points

• Lord Cornwallis introduced the Zamindari Settlement in 1793 as a measure of land revenue administration in British India.

• The Zamindari Settlement was a system of land revenue collection where the East India Company granted the zamindars (landlords) the right to collect revenue from the peasants in exchange for a fixed amount of revenue paid to the Company.

• The system was criticized for its exploitation of peasants by the zamindars and for perpetuating the feudal system in India.

Additional Information

• Lord Lytton introduced the infamous Vernacular Press Act in 1878, which curbed the freedom of the press in India and led to widespread protests.

• Lord Curzon was known for his administrative reforms in India, including the partition of Bengal in 1905, which sparked nationalist movements.

questions.q: A family income is Rs. 35,000 in a month. The family spends the income on various expenditures, viz., food, health, education, entertainment, and rent. After incurring all the expenditures, 8% is saved every month. The expenditure on health is 50% more than that of food. While food is three times of the expenditure on entertainment, the expenditure on health is half of the expenditure on education. The expenditure on rent is one-third of the combined expenditure on food, health and education. How much expenditure (in Rs.) is incurred on education?
questions.solution:
Given:

The monthly income of the family = Rs.35000

Saving after expenditure = 35000 × 8% = 2800

Expenditure = (35000 - 2800) = Rs.32200

Expenditure on food : expenditure on health = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

Expenditure on food : expenditure on entertainment = 3 : 1

Expenditure on health : expenditure on education = 1 : 2

Expenditure on rent : combined expenditure of (food + health + education) = 1 : 3

Concept used:

A : B = P : Q; B : C = R : S

A : B : C = PR : QR : QS

Calculation:

Exp. on food : exp. on health : exp. on entertainment : exp. on education = 6 : 9 : 2 : 18

Exp. on rent : combined exp. of (food + health + education) = (1 : 3) × 11 = 11 : 33

Exp. on food : exp. on health : exp. on entertainment : exp. on education : exp. on rent = 6 : 9 : 2 : 18 : 11

Now, (6 + 9 + 2 + 18 + 11) units = 46 units = 32200

⇒ 1 unit = 32200/46 = Rs.700

Exp. on education = 18 units = 700 × 18 = Rs.12600

∴ The correct answer is Rs.12600.
